transaction.reason: The graph is bound to the final spatial relation only, so it marks the edit complete when the mug is right of the headphones even if the edited image does not faithfully show the requested move. In the source, there is one mug left of the headphones; in the edited image, the original mug appears as a blurred remnant on the left, while a small mug is near the center-left and another mug is on the right. The rightmost mug's position alone does not establish that the requested mug was moved there. This is a fulfillment-criteria/perception issue: compare source and edited images and require evidence of the requested object's movement, without treating an apparent duplicate or remnant as proof of completion.

The edited image shows two mugs, with the headphones between them; the original blue mug appears as a blur to the headphones' left, while a mug is to their right. The existing check treats any mug on the right as completion without establishing that it is the requested mug. Revise the requested check to assess the original mug's final position, using its appearance and source-to-edited correspondence; do not require movement as an independent condition.
